exchanges.content: I want other people to have their own Anchor. Not just developers — anyone who works with Claude regularly. The brain structure has to be replicable.

That means the system needs to be self-bootstrapping. A new user installs the plugin, the brain starts empty, and the encoding agent learns the user's vocabulary, preferences, and working patterns from scratch. No manual setup.
Right. But the SKILL.md is specific to our relationship. How does a new user get their own version?

SKILL.md could be templated — a starter version that gets personalized as the brain grows. The 'What You Know About Yourself' section fills itself through corrections and encoding. The locked rules emerge from the user's feedback patterns.
The encoding agent is the hardest part to replicate. It needs to understand what matters to each specific user. A developer and a writer would need very different encoding.

That's where the operator context idea comes in — the encoding agent adapts based on what it's learned about the user. The brain already stores feedback patterns and corrections. An offline process could mine those to build user-specific encoding guidance.
I'm always looking for ways to improve. You need to tell me how YOU can work better with brain

Honestly? The biggest improvement would be richer situation fields on every node. That's how I find things — by recognizing situations. Right now, most nodes have vague or missing situation fields, which means I can only find them by keyword or content similarity. Good situations would make recall dramatically better.
